Chapter 25
What Fortune Can Effect In Human Affairs And How To Withstand Her

I know that many people have believed, and still believe, that God and fortune control the world's affairs. They think human wisdom cannot change how things play out, and that our efforts are ultimately useless. Because of this, they argue that we should not sweat the details, but simply let chance run its course. This belief has grown stronger in our own times. We have witnessed immense and unpredictable upheavals happening every single day, completely defying human imagination. Sometimes, when I think about this, I find myself somewhat agreeing with them. Nevertheless, we cannot let our free will be entirely extinguished. I believe the truth is that Fortuna controls about half of our actions. But she still leaves us to direct the other half, or perhaps just a little less.

I compare Fortuna to one of those raging, destructive rivers. When it floods, it overflows the plains, sweeps away trees and buildings, and tears the soil from one place to dump it in another. Everyone runs from it. Everyone yields to its violent fury, completely unable to stop it. Yet, even though rivers act this way, it does not mean men are helpless. When the weather is calm, people can build defenses, dams, and barriers. That way, when the waters rise again, the flood will be channeled through canals. Its force will no longer be so wild or dangerous. The exact same thing happens with Fortuna. She shows her crushing power wherever no Virtù has been prepared to resist her. She directs her fury exactly where she knows no barriers or defenses have been built to hold her back.

Now look at Italy. It is the epicenter of these massive political changes, and it is the very place that set them in motion. You will see that Italy is an open country, completely stripped of barriers and lacking any defense. If it had been defended by the proper Virtù, just like Germany, Spain, and France, things would have been different. Either these foreign invasions would not have caused such massive upheavals, or they would never have happened in the first place. I consider this enough to say about resisting fortune in general.

But zooming in on the specifics, we often see a prince thriving today and utterly ruined tomorrow, even though his character and behavior have not changed at all. I believe this happens first for the reasons we have already discussed at length. Namely, a prince who relies entirely on fortune will be destroyed the moment his luck changes. I also believe that a leader will only succeed if he adapts his actions to the spirit of the times. If his methods clash with the current era, he will fail. Men all want the same ultimate goals: glory and wealth. Yet we see them trying to get there using completely different methods. One moves with caution, while another rushes in. One uses brute force, and another uses clever skill. One is incredibly patient, while another is exactly the opposite. Surprisingly, each of these totally different methods can lead to success. You can also look at two cautious men: one achieves his goal, and the other fails completely. Similarly, you can see two men succeed equally well using opposite strategies, with one being cautious and the other aggressive. Why does this happen? It all comes down to whether or not their methods fit the spirit of the times. This proves my point. Two men can act differently and get the exact same result. Meanwhile, two men can act exactly the same way, but one achieves his goal while the other fails.

The rise and fall of a prince's power also depends on this principle. Suppose a prince rules with caution and patience. If the times and circumstances demand those exact traits, he will be highly successful. His fortune is made. But if the times change, he will be ruined unless he changes his strategy to match. The problem is, you rarely find a man flexible enough to adapt to these shifts. This is partly because a man cannot easily go against his own nature. It is also because, if a man has always succeeded by acting a certain way, you can never convince him to abandon that winning formula. So, when the time comes for the cautious man to be aggressive, he has no idea how to do it. As a result, he is destroyed. If he could have only changed his character to match the times, his fortune would never have turned against him.

Take Pope Julius the Second as an example. He acted aggressively and impulsively in everything he did. Fortunately for him, the times and circumstances matched his bold nature so perfectly that he always succeeded. Consider his first military campaign against Bologna, while Messer Giovanni Bentivogli was still alive. The Venetians opposed this move. So did the King of Spain. Julius was even still negotiating the plan with the King of France. Despite all this hesitation, he personally marched into battle with his usual relentless energy. This sudden, bold move completely paralyzed Spain and the Venetians. The Venetians froze out of fear, while Spain held back because they wanted to recover the kingdom of Naples. At the same time, Julius forced the King of France's hand. Seeing the Pope already making a move, the French King realized he needed the Pope as an ally to crush the Venetians. It became impossible for France to refuse him military support. Through sheer reckless aggression, Julius achieved what no other Pope could have managed with all the careful human wisdom in the world. If he had waited safely in Rome to organize his plans and secure his alliances, like any normal Pope would have done, he would have failed completely. The King of France would have invented a thousand excuses, and everyone else would have raised a thousand fears.

I will skip over his other actions, as they all followed the same aggressive pattern, and they all succeeded. His short life meant he never had to experience the harsh flip side of this coin. If times had changed and required him to act with caution, he would have been utterly ruined. He would never have been able to change the aggressive nature he was born with.

I conclude, therefore, that Fortuna is always changing, while men remain stubborn in their ways. As long as a man's nature perfectly aligns with Fortuna, he will be wildly successful. But the moment they fall out of sync, he will fail miserably. Personally, I believe it is always better to be aggressive than cautious. Fortuna is a woman, and if you want to keep her under your control, you have to beat her and force her into submission. History shows she is much more willing to let herself be mastered by bold, aggressive men than by those who act coldly and carefully. Because she is a woman, she is always drawn to young men. They are less cautious, more violent, and they command her with absolute audacity.
